root.label: Linear Algebra
root.summary: The study of vectors and linear functions, focusing on organizing information about vector spaces to make problems involving linear functions of many variables tractable.

vectors_concept.label: Vectors
vectors_concept.summary: Objects that can be added together and multiplied by scalars. They are not limited to stacks of numbers but include any mathematical object following these rules.

vector_examples.label: Examples of Vectors
vector_examples.summary: Diverse mathematical objects that function as vectors because they support addition and scalar multiplication.

fact_vec_numbers.label: Numbers as Vectors
fact_vec_numbers.summary: Real numbers can be treated as vectors where addition and scalar multiplication are standard arithmetic operations. (Page 12)

fact_vec_n_vectors.label: n-Vectors as Vectors
fact_vec_n_vectors.summary: Ordered lists of numbers (stacks) that can be added component-wise. (Page 12)

fact_vec_polynomials.label: Polynomials as Vectors
fact_vec_polynomials.summary: Polynomials are vectors where addition is performed by summing coefficients of like terms. (Page 12)

fact_vec_power_series.label: Power Series as Vectors
fact_vec_power_series.summary: Infinite series that can be added together term by term. (Page 12)

fact_vec_functions.label: Functions as Vectors
fact_vec_functions.summary: Functions mapping a domain to a codomain, where addition is pointwise: (f+g)(x) = f(x) + g(x). (Page 12)

zero_vector.label: Zero Vector
zero_vector.summary: A special vector produced by scalar multiplying any vector by 0, denoted as 0.

fact_zero_vec_def.label: Zero Vector Definition
fact_zero_vec_def.summary: The zero vector is the additive identity; for any vector v, v + 0 = v. It varies by the type of vector space (e.g., zero polynomial, zero function). (Page 14)

linear_functions_concept.label: Linear Functions
linear_functions_concept.summary: Functions of vectors that respect vector addition and scalar multiplication, also known as linear transformations or linear operators.

linearity_properties.label: Properties of Linearity
linearity_properties.summary: The two essential characteristics that define a linear function.

fact_additivity.label: Additivity
fact_additivity.summary: L(u + v) = L(u) + L(v). The function respects vector addition. (Page 18)

fact_homogeneity.label: Homogeneity
fact_homogeneity.summary: L(cu) = cL(u). The function respects scalar multiplication. (Page 18)

fact_linearity_combined.label: Combined Linearity
fact_linearity_combined.summary: L(cu + dv) = cL(u) + dL(v). This property allows linear functions to be specified by their action on a basis. (Page 20)

linear_operator_examples.label: Examples of Linear Operators
linear_operator_examples.summary: Real-world and mathematical instances of linear transformations.

fact_derivative_operator.label: The Derivative Operator
fact_derivative_operator.summary: The operator d/dx is linear because d/dx(cf + g) = c(df/dx) + dg/dx. (Page 19)

matrices_concept.label: Matrices
matrices_concept.summary: Arrays of numbers used to organize information about linear functions; they represent linear transformations under specific notational choices (bases).

matrix_vector_multiplication.label: Matrix-Vector Multiplication
matrix_vector_multiplication.summary: A process where a matrix acts on a vector to produce another vector, equivalent to a linear combination of the matrix columns. (Page 22)

fact_col_space_def.label: Column Space
fact_col_space_def.summary: The set of all possible outputs of a matrix times a vector; also known as the image of the linear function. (Page 23)

matrix_multiplication.label: Matrix Multiplication
matrix_multiplication.summary: The multiplication of two matrices, which corresponds to the composition of their respective linear functions.

fact_composition_def.label: Composition of Functions
fact_composition_def.summary: If f: U -> V and g: V -> W, the composition g o f: U -> W is defined by (g o f)(u) = g(f(u)). Matrix multiplication computes this. (Page 25)

matrix_invertibility.label: Matrix Invertibility
matrix_invertibility.summary: A property of square matrices that allow them to be 'undone'.

fact_invertible_def.label: Invertible Matrix Definition
fact_invertible_def.summary: A matrix M is invertible if its Reduced Row Echelon Form (RREF) is the identity matrix I. (Page 55)

fact_inverse_property.label: Inverse Matrix Property
fact_inverse_property.summary: Two matrices M and N are inverses if MN = I and NM = I, denoted as N = M^-1. (Page 55)

matrix_factorizations.label: Matrix Factorizations
matrix_factorizations.summary: Decomposing a matrix into a product of simpler matrices (e.g., triangular matrices).

fact_lu_decomp.label: LU Decomposition
fact_lu_decomp.summary: Factorizing a matrix M into M = LU, where L is lower triangular and U is upper triangular. (Page 58)

fact_ldu_decomp.label: LDU Decomposition
fact_ldu_decomp.summary: A refinement of LU where M = LDU; L is lower triangular with 1s on the diagonal, D is diagonal, and U is upper triangular with 1s on the diagonal. (Page 60)

fact_pldu_decomp.label: PLDU Decomposition
fact_pldu_decomp.summary: Used when row exchanges are necessary: M = PLDU, where P is a permutation matrix. (Page 61)

systems_linear_equations.label: Systems of Linear Equations
systems_linear_equations.summary: Collections of equations where variables are multiplied by constants and summed. They can be represented as matrix equations Mv = w.

gaussian_elimination.label: Gaussian Elimination
gaussian_elimination.summary: An algorithm for simplifying systems of linear equations using augmented matrices and elementary row operations.

augmented_matrix.label: Augmented Matrix
augmented_matrix.summary: A notation that combines the coefficient matrix and the constants vector into one matrix for efficient computation. (Page 37)

ero_concept.label: Elementary Row Operations (EROs)
ero_concept.summary: Operations that simplify a matrix without changing the solution set of the associated system.

fact_ero_swap.label: Row Swap
fact_ero_swap.summary: Interchanging any two rows of a matrix. (Page 42)

fact_ero_scalar.label: Scalar Multiplication
fact_ero_scalar.summary: Multiplying a row by a non-zero constant. (Page 42)

fact_ero_addition.label: Row Addition
fact_ero_addition.summary: Adding one row to another row. (Page 42)

rref_concept.label: Reduced Row Echelon Form (RREF)
rref_concept.summary: The most simplified form of a matrix reachable via EROs.

fact_rref_prop1.label: RREF Property 1
fact_rref_prop1.summary: In every row, the leftmost non-zero entry is 1 (the pivot). (Page 44)

fact_rref_prop2.label: RREF Property 2
fact_rref_prop2.summary: The pivot of any given row is always to the right of the pivot of the row above it. (Page 44)

fact_rref_prop3.label: RREF Property 3
fact_rref_prop3.summary: The pivot is the only non-zero entry in its column. (Page 44)

solution_sets_sle.label: Solution Sets for SLE
solution_sets_sle.summary: The set of all vectors that satisfy a system of linear equations.

fact_sol_types.label: Possible Solution Outcomes
fact_sol_types.summary: A linear system Ax = b has either one solution, no solutions, or infinitely many solutions. (Page 63)

particular_homogeneous_solutions.label: Particular and Homogeneous Solutions
particular_homogeneous_solutions.summary: The general solution to a linear system is the sum of a particular solution and the set of homogeneous solutions.

fact_particular_sol.label: Particular Solution
fact_particular_sol.summary: A specific vector x_p that satisfies M x_p = v. (Page 47)

fact_homogeneous_sol.label: Homogeneous Solution
fact_homogeneous_sol.summary: A vector x_H that satisfies M x_H = 0, where 0 is the zero vector. (Page 47)

simplex_method.label: The Simplex Method
simplex_method.summary: A computational algorithm for solving linear programming problems to find an optimal solution under linear constraints.

linear_programming.label: Linear Programming
linear_programming.summary: The process of maximizing or minimizing a linear objective function subject to linear inequalities (constraints).

fact_feasible_region.label: Feasible Region
fact_feasible_region.summary: The set of all variable values that satisfy all constraints of a linear programming problem. (Page 73)

fact_vertex_optimality.label: Vertex Optimality
fact_vertex_optimality.summary: The optimal answer to a linear programming problem must lie at a vertex of the feasible region. (Page 73)

simplex_algorithm_details.label: Simplex Algorithm Details
simplex_algorithm_details.summary: The mechanics of Dantzig's algorithm using augmented matrices and slack/artificial variables.

fact_slack_variables.label: Slack Variables
fact_slack_variables.summary: Positive variables introduced to convert linear inequalities into linear equalities (e.g., x + y <= 13 becomes x + y + s = 13). (Page 78)

fact_artificial_variables.label: Artificial Variables
fact_artificial_variables.summary: Variables added to constraints to facilitate the start of the simplex algorithm, which are then forced to zero using a penalty in the objective function. (Page 79)

n_vectors_space.label: Vectors in Space (Rn)
n_vectors_space.summary: The study of n-dimensional Euclidean space consisting of all n-vectors.

hyperplanes_concept.label: Hyperplanes
hyperplanes_concept.summary: Generalizations of lines and planes in higher dimensions.

fact_hyperplane_def.label: k-Dimensional Hyperplane
fact_hyperplane_def.summary: A set of points defined by P + sum(lambda_i * v_i) for i=1 to k, where v_i are vectors not lying in the (k-1)-dimensional hyperplane determined by the others. (Page 86)

fact_standard_hyperplane.label: Standard Hyperplane
fact_standard_hyperplane.summary: Unless specified, a 'hyperplane' in Rn refers to a (n-1)-dimensional hyperplane, typically defined by a single linear algebraic equation. (Page 87)

euclidean_metrics.label: Euclidean Metrics
euclidean_metrics.summary: The tools used to measure lengths, angles, and orthogonality in Rn.

dot_product.label: Dot Product
dot_product.summary: An algebraic operation that takes two equal-length sequences of numbers and returns a single number.

fact_dot_product_props.label: Dot Product Properties
fact_dot_product_props.summary: The dot product is symmetric, distributive, bilinear, and positive definite. (Page 91)

vector_norm.label: Vector Norm (Length)
vector_norm.summary: The Euclidean length of a vector.

vector_angle.label: Vector Angle
vector_angle.summary: The angle theta between two vectors determined by their dot product and norms.

orthogonal_vectors.label: Orthogonal Vectors
orthogonal_vectors.summary: Vectors that are perpendicular to each other.

fact_orthogonality_def.label: Orthogonality Definition
fact_orthogonality_def.summary: Two vectors are orthogonal if their dot product is zero. (Page 90)

rs_notation.label: RS Notation
rs_notation.summary: Viewing n-vectors as functions from a set S to the real numbers.

fact_rs_def.label: RS Definition
fact_rs_def.summary: RS is the set of all functions f: S -> R. When S = {1, ..., n}, RS is equivalent to Rn. (Page 95)

vector_spaces_general.label: Vector Spaces (General)
vector_spaces_general.summary: A formal mathematical structure consisting of a set closed under addition and scalar multiplication satisfying ten axioms.

vector_space_axioms.label: Vector Space Axioms
vector_space_axioms.summary: The ten rules that must be satisfied for a set V to be a vector space over a field.

fact_ax_add_closure.label: Additive Closure
fact_ax_add_closure.summary: u + v is in V for all u, v in V. (Page 101)

fact_ax_zero.label: Zero Vector Existence
fact_ax_zero.summary: There exists 0 such that u + 0 = u. (Page 101)

fact_ax_add_inv.label: Additive Inverse Existence
fact_ax_add_inv.summary: For every u, there exists w such that u + w = 0. (Page 101)

fact_ax_mult_closure.label: Multiplicative Closure
fact_ax_mult_closure.summary: cv is in V for all scalars c and vectors v. (Page 101)

vector_space_examples.label: Examples of Vector Spaces
vector_space_examples.summary: Common sets that satisfy the vector space axioms.

fact_vs_rn.label: Rn Space
fact_vs_rn.summary: The set of all n-vectors over the field of real numbers. (Page 102)

fact_vs_sequences.label: Sequence Space (RN)
fact_vs_sequences.summary: The set of functions from natural numbers to real numbers, viewed as infinite lists. (Page 102)

fact_vs_diff_funcs.label: Differentiable Function Space
fact_vs_diff_funcs.summary: The set of functions that have at least one derivative. (Page 104)

subspace_concept.label: Subspace
subspace_concept.summary: A vector space that is a subset of another vector space.

fact_subspace_def.label: Subspace Definition
fact_subspace_def.summary: A subset is a subspace if it is closed under addition and scalar multiplication. (Page 105)

fact_homogeneous_sol_subspace.label: Homogeneous Solution Subspace
fact_homogeneous_sol_subspace.summary: The solution set to a homogeneous linear equation Mx = 0 is always a subspace, called the kernel of M. (Page 105)

base_fields.label: Base Fields
base_fields.summary: The set of scalars used in a vector space.

fact_field_real.label: Real Field (R)
fact_field_real.summary: The standard field of real numbers. (Page 107)

fact_field_complex.label: Complex Field (C)
fact_field_complex.summary: Numbers of the form x + iy. Useful because every polynomial over C factors into linear polynomials. (Page 107)

fact_field_rational.label: Rational Field (Q)
fact_field_rational.summary: Numbers expressed as fractions, used in computer algebra for precision. (Page 108)

fact_field_bits.label: Bit Field (Z2)
fact_field_bits.summary: The set {0, 1} where addition and multiplication follow binary logic (e.g., 1 + 1 = 0). (Page 108)

linear_transformations.label: Linear Transformations
linear_transformations.summary: Functions between vector spaces that preserve addition and scalar multiplication.

linearity_definition.label: Linearity Definition
linearity_definition.summary: The core properties that define a linear function.

fact_linearity_conditions.label: Linearity Conditions
fact_linearity_conditions.summary: L(u + v) = L(u) + L(v) and L(cv) = cL(v) for all vectors u, v and scalar c.

fact_linearity_equivalent.label: Linearity Equivalent Form
fact_linearity_equivalent.summary: The two conditions of linearity are equivalent to the single condition: L(ru + sv) = rL(u) + sL(v) (p. 118).

matrix_representation_of_L.label: Matrix Representation of L
matrix_representation_of_L.summary: The process of encoding a linear operator as a matrix given specific bases.

fact_matrix_dimensions.label: Matrix Dimensions
fact_matrix_dimensions.summary: A linear transformation L: V -> W is represented by an m x n matrix where n is the dimension of the domain V and m is the dimension of the codomain W (p. 114).

fact_matrix_construction.label: Matrix Construction Process
fact_matrix_construction.summary: To calculate the matrix of a linear transformation, compute what the transformation does to every input basis vector and write the results in terms of the output basis vectors (p. 127).

linear_differential_operators.label: Linear Differential Operators
linear_differential_operators.summary: Differential operators acting on function spaces, such as polynomials, which obey linearity.

fact_derivative_basis_action.label: Derivative Basis Action
fact_derivative_basis_action.summary: The derivative operator d/dx acting on polynomials of degree 2 or less is completely determined by its action on the basis {1, x, x^2}: d/dx(1)=0, d/dx(x)=1, d/dx(x^2)=2x (p. 115).

bases_dimension.label: Bases and Dimension
bases_dimension.summary: Systems for uniquely labeling vectors in a vector space and the measure of a space's size.

basis_definition.label: Basis Definition
basis_definition.summary: A set of vectors in which it is possible to uniquely express any other vector in the space (p. 118).

fact_basis_invertibility.label: Basis and Invertibility
fact_basis_invertibility.summary: A pair or triple of vectors forms a basis for R2 or R3 if they, when used as columns of a matrix, give an invertible matrix (p. 117).

dimension_definition.label: Dimension Definition
dimension_definition.summary: The number of independent directions available in a vector space; specifically, the number of vectors in any basis for that space (p. 117).

fact_dim_invariant.label: Dimension Invariance
fact_dim_invariant.summary: All bases for a particular vector space have the same number of vectors (p. 117).

standard_basis.label: Standard Basis
standard_basis.summary: The canonical basis for Rn consisting of vectors ei with 1 at index i and 0 elsewhere (p. 122, 216).

basis_transformation.label: Basis Transformation/Notation
basis_transformation.summary: Expressing vectors as column vectors relative to a specific basis.

fact_column_vector_notation.label: Column Vector Notation
fact_column_vector_notation.summary: The column vector [v]_B consists of coefficients (alpha1, ..., alphan) such that v = sum(alpha_i * b_i) (p. 126).

matrices.label: Matrices
matrices.summary: Rectangular arrays of numbers used as a tool for calculating linear transformations.

matrix_operations.label: Matrix Operations
matrix_operations.summary: Standard algebraic operations performed on matrices.

fact_matrix_multiplication_rule.label: Matrix Multiplication Rule
fact_matrix_multiplication_rule.summary: The entry L_ij of the product MN is the dot product of the i-th row of M and the j-th column of N: sum_{p=1}^k M_ip * N_pj (p. 136, 137).

fact_matrix_multiplication_properties.label: Matrix Multiplication Properties
fact_matrix_multiplication_properties.summary: Matrix multiplication is associative (M(NR) = (MN)R) but generally non-commutative (MN != NM) (p. 140, 141).

fact_transpose_rule.label: Transpose Rule
fact_transpose_rule.summary: The transpose M^T swaps rows and columns. Property: (MN)^T = N^T M^T (p. 134, 139).

fact_trace_definition.label: Trace Definition
fact_trace_definition.summary: The trace of a square matrix is the sum of its diagonal entries: tr(M) = sum(m_ii) (p. 145).

fact_trace_property.label: Trace Property
fact_trace_property.summary: The trace of a product is independent of order: tr(MN) = tr(NM) (p. 145).

elementary_matrices.label: Elementary Matrices
elementary_matrices.summary: Matrices that perform a single elementary row operation (ERO).

ero_swap.label: Row Swap Matrix
ero_swap.summary: Ei,j is the identity matrix with rows i and j swapped. det(Ei,j) = -1 (p. 174, 175).

ero_multiplication.label: Row Multiplication Matrix
ero_multiplication.summary: Ri(lambda) is the identity matrix with the i-th diagonal entry replaced by lambda. det(Ri(lambda)) = lambda (p. 176).

ero_addition.label: Row Addition Matrix
ero_addition.summary: Si,j(mu) is the identity matrix with mu in the i,j position. det(Si,j(mu)) = 1 (p. 177, 178).

matrix_inverses.label: Matrix Inverses
matrix_inverses.summary: The process of finding a matrix M^-1 such that M M^-1 = I.

fact_invertibility_condition.label: Invertibility Condition
fact_invertibility_condition.summary: A square matrix M is invertible (non-singular) iff the homogeneous system Mx = 0 has only the trivial solution x = 0 (p. 154).

fact_inverse_gaussian.label: Inverse via Gaussian Elimination
fact_inverse_gaussian.summary: M^-1 can be found by augmenting M with the identity matrix [M | I] and row-reducing to [I | M^-1] (p. 152).

bit_matrices.label: Bit Matrices
bit_matrices.summary: Matrices with entries in Z2 = {0, 1}, where addition and multiplication follow binary field rules (p. 154, 155).

matrix_decompositions.label: Matrix Decompositions
matrix_decompositions.summary: Breaking a matrix into a product of simpler matrices to facilitate computation.

lu_decomposition.label: LU Decomposition
lu_decomposition.summary: M = LU, where L is lower triangular (entries above diagonal are 0) and U is upper triangular (entries below diagonal are 0) (p. 159).

fact_lu_solving_steps.label: Solving via LU
fact_lu_solving_steps.summary: To solve MX = V, first solve LW = V for W via forward substitution, then solve UX = W for X via back substitution (p. 160).

ldu_decomposition.label: LDU Decomposition
ldu_decomposition.summary: Decomposition into a unit lower triangular matrix L, a diagonal matrix D, and a unit upper triangular matrix U (p. 165).

determinants.label: Determinants
determinants.summary: A scalar value that characterizes a square matrix and determines its invertibility.

det_definition.label: Determinant Definition
det_definition.summary: det M = sum_{sigma} sgn(sigma) * product(m_i, sigma(i)), summed over all permutations sigma of n objects (p. 172).

fact_det_invertibility.label: Determinant and Invertibility
fact_det_invertibility.summary: A square matrix M is invertible if and only if det M != 0 (p. 180).

fact_det_row_swap.label: Determinant Row Swap
fact_det_row_swap.summary: Swapping two rows of a matrix flips the sign of the determinant (p. 173, 174).

fact_det_row_scale.label: Determinant Row Scaling
fact_det_row_scale.summary: Multiplying a row by scalar lambda multiplies the determinant by lambda (p. 176, 177).

det_calculation_methods.label: Determinant Calculation
det_calculation_methods.summary: Techniques to compute det M beyond the general permutation formula.

fact_det_diagonal.label: Determinant of Diagonal Matrix
fact_det_diagonal.summary: The determinant of a diagonal matrix is the product of its diagonal entries (p. 173).

fact_expansion_by_minors.label: Expansion by Minors
fact_expansion_by_minors.summary: Expanding the determinant along a row/column by summing (-1)^(i+j) * m_ij * det(Minor_ij) (p. 186, 187).

adjunct_matrix.label: Adjoint Matrix
adjunct_matrix.summary: The transpose of the cofactor matrix, used to find the inverse of a matrix.

symmetric_matrix.label: Symmetric Matrix
symmetric_matrix.summary: A square matrix where M = M^T (p. 139).

diagonal_matrix.label: Diagonal Matrix
diagonal_matrix.summary: A square matrix where all non-diagonal entries are zero (p. 138).

identity_matrix.label: Identity Matrix
identity_matrix.summary: A diagonal matrix with all diagonal entries equal to 1; serves as the multiplicative identity (p. 139).

block_matrix.label: Block Matrix
block_matrix.summary: A matrix partitioned into smaller matrices called blocks, allowing operations to be carried out on the blocks themselves (p. 142, 143).

subspaces_spanning.label: Subspaces and Spanning Sets
subspaces_spanning.summary: The study of subsets of vector spaces that maintain vector space properties.

subspace_definition.label: Subspace Definition
subspace_definition.summary: A subset U of vector space V is a subspace if it is closed under addition and scalar multiplication (p. 195).

fact_subspace_theorem.label: Subspace Theorem
fact_subspace_theorem.summary: A non-empty subset U is a subspace iff mu*u1 + nu*u2 is in U for all u1, u2 in U and constants mu, nu (p. 196).

span_definition.label: Span Definition
span_definition.summary: The span of a set S is the set of all finite linear combinations of elements of S (p. 198).

fact_span_is_subspace.label: Span as Subspace
fact_span_is_subspace.summary: For any subset S of V, span(S) is a subspace of V (p. 199).

linear_map_subspaces.label: Linear Map Subspaces
linear_map_subspaces.summary: Specific subspaces derived from linear transformations.

kernel_definition.label: Kernel (ker L)
kernel_definition.summary: The set of all vectors in the domain that map to the zero vector: {u in U | L(u) = 0} (p. 200).

image_definition.label: Image (im L)
image_definition.summary: The set of all vectors in the codomain that are outputs of the map: {L(u) | u in U} (p. 201).

eigenspace_definition.label: Eigenspace (V_lambda)
eigenspace_definition.summary: The set of all vectors that obey the eigenvector equation L(v) = lambda*v (p. 201).

linear_independence.label: Linear Independence
linear_independence.summary: The property of a set of vectors where no vector can be expressed as a linear combination of the others.

linear_dependence_definition.label: Linear Dependence Definition
linear_dependence_definition.summary: Vectors v1...vn are linearly dependent if there exist constants c1...cn, not all zero, such that sum(ci*vi) = 0 (p. 204).

fact_dependence_linear_comb.label: Dependence and Linear Combinations
fact_dependence_linear_comb.summary: A set of non-zero vectors is linearly dependent iff one of the vectors is expressible as a linear combination of the preceding vectors (p. 205).

linear_independence_definition.label: Linear Independence Definition
linear_independence_definition.summary: Vectors are linearly independent if the only solution to sum(ci*vi) = 0 is ci = 0 for all i (p. 204).

fact_independence_zero_vector.label: Zero Vector and Independence
fact_independence_zero_vector.summary: The zero vector can never be part of a linearly independent set (p. 204).

eigen_theory.label: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
eigen_theory.summary: The study of invariant directions of linear operators.

eigenvalue_equation.label: Eigenvalue-Eigenvector Equation
eigenvalue_equation.summary: L(v) = lambda * v, where v is a non-zero eigenvector and lambda is the eigenvalue (p. 227, 229).

characteristic_polynomial.label: Characteristic Polynomial
characteristic_polynomial.summary: The polynomial P_M(lambda) = det(lambda*I - M), whose roots are the eigenvalues of M (p. 232).

diagonalization.label: Diagonalization
diagonalization.summary: The process of finding a basis of eigenvectors such that the matrix representation of L is a diagonal matrix containing the eigenvalues (p. 230).

concept_eigen.label: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
concept_eigen.summary: The study of scalars and vectors that characterize the scaling behavior of a linear transformation.

sub_char_poly.label: Characteristic Polynomial
sub_char_poly.summary: The polynomial PM(λ) used to find eigenvalues of a matrix M.

fact_char_poly_def.label: Characteristic Polynomial Definition
fact_char_poly_def.summary: Defined as det(λI - M) = 0 or det(M - λI) = 0 (Page 234).

fact_char_poly_deg.label: Polynomial Degree
fact_char_poly_deg.summary: For an n x n matrix, the characteristic polynomial has degree n (Page 234).

sub_eigenvalue.label: Eigenvalues
sub_eigenvalue.summary: The roots of the characteristic polynomial.

fact_eigenvalue_def.label: Eigenvalue Definition
fact_eigenvalue_def.summary: Complex numbers λi such that PM(λi) = 0. They can be real, complex, or zero (Page 234).

fact_fta.label: Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
fact_fta.summary: Any polynomial can be factored into a product of first order polynomials over C (Page 234).

fact_multiplicity.label: Multiplicity
fact_multiplicity.summary: The number of times a given root λi appears in the collection of eigenvalues (Page 234).

sub_eigenvector.label: Eigenvectors
sub_eigenvector.summary: Non-zero vectors that are scaled by the linear transformation.

fact_eigenvector_def.label: Eigenvector Definition
fact_eigenvector_def.summary: A vector X such that MX = λX or (M - λI)X = 0 (Page 235).

fact_eigenvector_sys.label: Homogeneous System
fact_eigenvector_sys.summary: Finding eigenvectors involves solving the homogeneous system (M - λiI)X = 0 for each eigenvalue (Page 235).

sub_eigenspace.label: Eigenspaces
sub_eigenspace.summary: The set of all vectors associated with a specific eigenvalue.

fact_eigenspace_def.label: Eigenspace Definition
fact_eigenspace_def.summary: The space of all vectors with eigenvalue λ; any linear combination of eigenvectors sharing the same eigenvalue is also an eigenvector (Page 237).

fact_eigenspace_subspace.label: Eigenspace as Subspace
fact_eigenspace_subspace.summary: Vλ := {v ∈ V | Lv = λv} is a subspace of V (Page 237).

concept_diag.label: Diagonalization
concept_diag.summary: The process of finding a basis of eigenvectors to represent a linear transformation as a diagonal matrix.

sub_diag_def.label: Diagonalizability
sub_diag_def.summary: The conditions under which a matrix can be represented as a diagonal matrix.

fact_diag_def.label: Diagonalizable Definition
fact_diag_def.summary: A linear transformation L is diagonalizable if there exists a collection of n linearly independent eigenvectors for L, forming a basis for V (Page 242).

fact_diag_theorem.label: Diagonal Matrix Theorem
fact_diag_theorem.summary: The matrix for L in basis B is diagonal if and only if B consists of eigenvectors for L (Page 242).

sub_change_basis.label: Change of Basis
sub_change_basis.summary: The mechanism for shifting a linear transformation's matrix representation between different bases.

fact_cob_matrix.label: Change of Basis Matrix P
fact_cob_matrix.summary: A square matrix where columns are the components of the new basis vectors in terms of the old basis vectors (Page 243).

fact_cob_formula.label: Change of Basis Formula
fact_cob_formula.summary: The new matrix M' is related to the old matrix M by M' = Q^-1 M P, where P and Q are change of basis matrices for input and output spaces (Page 245).

sub_similarity.label: Similarity
sub_similarity.summary: The relationship between two matrices that represent the same linear transformation in different bases.

fact_similar_def.label: Similar Matrices Definition
fact_similar_def.summary: Two matrices M and N are similar if there exists an invertible matrix P such that M = P^-1 N P (Page 247).

fact_diag_similarity.label: Diagonal Similarity
fact_diag_similarity.summary: A matrix is diagonalizable if and only if it is similar to a diagonal matrix D consisting of its eigenvalues (Page 247).

concept_ortho.label: Orthonormal Bases and Complements
concept_ortho.summary: Study of vector spaces equipped with an inner product, allowing for notions of length, angle, and perpendicularity.

sub_ortho_bases.label: Orthogonal and Orthonormal Bases
sub_ortho_bases.summary: Special types of bases where vectors are mutually perpendicular.

fact_ortho_basis_def.label: Orthogonal Basis Definition
fact_ortho_basis_def.summary: A basis where vi · vj = 0 if i != j (Page 255).

fact_orthonormal_basis_def.label: Orthonormal Basis Definition
fact_orthonormal_basis_def.summary: An orthogonal basis where every vector has unit length (ui · uj = δij) (Page 255).

fact_orthonormal_expansion.label: Orthonormal Expansion Theorem
fact_orthonormal_expansion.summary: Any vector v can be expressed as v = Σ(v · ui)ui for an orthonormal basis {ui} (Page 256).

sub_gram_schmidt.label: Gram-Schmidt Process
sub_gram_schmidt.summary: An algorithm for constructing an orthogonal basis from a set of linearly independent vectors.

fact_gs_step.label: Gram-Schmidt Projection Step
fact_gs_step.summary: Constructs orthogonal vectors by subtracting projections: v_i_perp = v_i - Σ[(v_i · v_j_perp)/(v_j_perp · v_j_perp)] v_j_perp (Page 264).

fact_gs_ortho_basis.label: GS Output
fact_gs_ortho_basis.summary: The process transforms a linearly independent set {v1...vn} into an orthogonal set {v1_perp...vn_perp} that spans the same space (Page 264).

sub_ortho_matrix.label: Orthogonal Matrices
sub_ortho_matrix.summary: Matrices whose columns form an orthonormal basis.

fact_ortho_mat_def.label: Orthogonal Matrix Definition
fact_ortho_mat_def.summary: A square matrix P is orthogonal if P^-1 = P^T (Page 259).

fact_ortho_mat_property.label: Orthogonal Matrix Property
fact_ortho_mat_property.summary: A change of basis matrix relating two orthonormal bases is always an orthogonal matrix (Page 260).

sub_ortho_complement.label: Orthogonal Complements
sub_ortho_complement.summary: The subspace consisting of all vectors orthogonal to a given subspace.

fact_ortho_comp_def.label: Orthogonal Complement Definition
fact_ortho_comp_def.summary: U^⊥ := {w ∈ W | <w, u> = 0 for all u ∈ U} (Page 269).

fact_direct_sum_decomp.label: Orthogonal Decomposition Theorem
fact_direct_sum_decomp.summary: For any subspace U of a finite-dimensional space W, W = U ⊕ U^⊥ (Page 270).

concept_sym.label: Symmetric Matrices
concept_sym.summary: Square matrices equal to their own transpose, possessing unique spectral properties.

sub_sym_def.label: Symmetric Matrix Definition
sub_sym_def.summary: A matrix M is symmetric if M^T = M (Page 277).

sub_sym_eig.label: Eigenproperties of Symmetric Matrices
sub_sym_eig.summary: Special results regarding the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of symmetric matrices.

fact_sym_real_eig.label: Reality of Eigenvalues
fact_sym_real_eig.summary: Symmetric matrices always have real eigenvalues (Page 277).

fact_sym_ortho_eig.label: Orthogonality of Eigenvectors
fact_sym_ortho_eig.summary: Eigenvectors of a symmetric matrix associated with distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal (Page 278).

sub_sym_diag.label: Symmetric Diagonalization
sub_sym_diag.summary: The ability to diagonalize symmetric matrices using orthogonal matrices.

fact_sym_diag_theorem.label: Symmetric Diagonalization Theorem
fact_sym_diag_theorem.summary: M = M^T if and only if M = P D P^T, where P is an orthogonal matrix and D is diagonal (Page 280).

concept_ker_ran.label: Kernel, Range, Nullity, and Rank
concept_ker_ran.summary: The fundamental subspaces associated with a linear transformation and the relationships between their dimensions.

sub_range.label: Range and Image
sub_range.summary: The set of all output vectors of a linear transformation.

fact_range_matrix.label: Range of a Matrix
fact_range_matrix.summary: The range of a matrix is the span of its columns (column space) (Page 286).

sub_kernel.label: Kernel
sub_kernel.summary: The set of all vectors that map to the zero vector.

fact_kernel_injectivity.label: Kernel and Injectivity
fact_kernel_injectivity.summary: A linear transformation L is injective if and only if ker L = {0_V} (Page 293).

sub_dim_formula.label: Rank-Nullity Theorem
sub_dim_formula.summary: The relationship between the dimension of the domain, the kernel, and the range.

fact_rank_def.label: Rank Definition
fact_rank_def.summary: The rank of L is the dimension of its range (dim ran L) (Page 295).

fact_nullity_def.label: Nullity Definition
fact_nullity_def.summary: The nullity of L is the dimension of its kernel (dim ker L) (Page 295).

fact_dim_formula.label: Dimension Formula
fact_dim_formula.summary: dim V = null L + rank L (Page 296).

concept_approx.label: Least Squares and Singular Values
concept_approx.summary: Techniques for approximating solutions to overdetermined systems and decomposing non-square matrices.

sub_least_squares.label: Least Squares Method
sub_least_squares.summary: Finding the x that minimizes the error ||Lx - v||.

fact_ls_normal_eq.label: Normal Equations
fact_ls_normal_eq.summary: Least squares solutions satisfy M^T M X = M^T V (Page 304).

sub_proj_matrix.label: Projection Matrices
sub_proj_matrix.summary: Matrices that project a vector onto a specific subspace.

fact_proj_formula.label: Projection Formula
fact_proj_formula.summary: The matrix projecting onto ran M is M(M^T M)^-1 M^T (Page 307).

sub_svd.label: Singular Value Decomposition
sub_svd.summary: A decomposition of any m x n matrix into orthogonal and diagonal components.

fact_svd_def.label: SVD Definition
fact_svd_def.summary: Decomposing M into QΣP^T where Q and P are orthogonal matrices and Σ contains singular values (Page 311).

fact_singular_values.label: Singular Values Definition
fact_singular_values.summary: The square roots of the eigenvalues of M^T M (Page 310).

concept_fields.label: Fields
concept_fields.summary: The algebraic structure providing the scalars for vector spaces.

fact_field_axioms.label: Field Axioms
fact_field_axioms.summary: A set with addition and multiplication obeying associativity, commutativity, identity, inverse, and distributivity (Page 316).

fact_field_examples.label: Common Fields
fact_field_examples.summary: Examples include Rational numbers (Q), Real numbers (R), Complex numbers (C), and Bit field (Z2) (Page 317).

sys_lin_eq.label: Systems of Linear Equations
sys_lin_eq.summary: Methods for representing and solving sets of linear equations using matrices.

aug_mat.label: Augmented Matrix Notation
aug_mat.summary: A compact notation for representing linear systems where coefficients and constants are stored together.

aug_equiv.label: Equivalence of Augmented Matrices
aug_equiv.summary: Two augmented matrices are equivalent if they represent systems with the same solution set.

row_equiv_fact.label: Row Equivalence Properties
row_equiv_fact.summary: Row equivalence is an equivalence relation satisfying reflexive, symmetric, and transitive properties.

gauss_elim.label: Gaussian Elimination
gauss_elim.summary: The process of using elementary row operations to transform a matrix into Row Echelon Form (REF) or Reduced Row Echelon Form (RREF).

ero_types.label: Elementary Row Operations (EROs)
ero_types.summary: Operations that do not change the solution set: swapping rows, scaling a row, and adding a multiple of one row to another.

pivot_vars.label: Pivot and Free Variables
pivot_vars.summary: Pivot variables correspond to leading ones in RREF; non-pivot variables are free variables used to parametrize the solution set.

sol_sets.label: Solution Sets
sol_sets.summary: The set of all vectors that satisfy a linear system, often expressed in parametric vector form.

inconsistent_fact.label: Inconsistent Systems
inconsistent_fact.summary: A system is inconsistent if a row of zeros precedes a non-vanishing entry in the augmented column (e.g., 0 = 6).

vec_spaces.label: Vector Spaces
vec_spaces.summary: Algebraic structures consisting of a set of vectors that can be added together and multiplied by scalars.

vs_axioms.label: Vector Space Axioms
vs_axioms.summary: The set of rules defining a vector space, divided into additive and multiplicative properties.

add_closure.label: Additive Closure
add_closure.summary: For any vectors u, v in V, u + v must also be in V.

add_comm.label: Additive Commutativity
add_comm.summary: u + v = v + u for all u, v in V.

add_assoc.label: Additive Associativity
add_assoc.summary: (u + v) + w = u + (v + w) for all u, v, w in V.

zero_vec.label: Zero Vector
zero_vec.summary: There exists a vector 0 such that v + 0 = v for all v in V.

add_inv.label: Additive Inverse
add_inv.summary: For every v in V, there exists -v such that v + (-v) = 0.

mul_closure.label: Multiplicative Closure
mul_closure.summary: For any scalar a and vector v, av must be in V.

subspaces.label: Subspaces
subspaces.summary: A subset of a vector space that is itself a vector space under the same operations.

subspace_sum.label: Subspace Sum
subspace_sum.summary: The sum of two subspaces U and V is the span of their union: U + V = span(U U V).

direct_sum.label: Direct Sum
direct_sum.summary: A subspace sum U + V where U intersection V = {0}, denoted as U ⊕ V.

ortho_complement.label: Orthogonal Complement
ortho_complement.summary: The set of all vectors perpendicular to every vector in a subspace U, denoted U⊩.

ortho_comp_fact.label: Complement Identity
ortho_comp_fact.summary: The orthogonal complement of an orthogonal complement returns the original subspace: (U⊩)⊩ = U.

basis_dim.label: Basis and Dimension
basis_dim.summary: A basis is a linearly independent spanning set; the dimension is the number of vectors in any basis.

lin_indep.label: Linear Independence
lin_indep.summary: A set of vectors is independent if the only solution to their linear combination equaling zero is the trivial solution.

spanning_set.label: Spanning Set
spanning_set.summary: A set of vectors whose linear combinations cover the entire vector space.

dim_formula.label: Dimension Formula
dim_formula.summary: Also known as the Rank-Nullity Theorem: dim V = dim(ker L) + dim(im L).

lin_trans.label: Linear Transformations
lin_trans.summary: Mappings between vector spaces that preserve vector addition and scalar multiplication.

kernel_range.label: Kernel and Range
kernel_range.summary: The kernel (null space) is the set of vectors mapped to zero; the range (image) is the set of all outputs.

bijectivity.label: Bijectivity and Invertibility
bijectivity.summary: A linear transformation L is bijective if and only if its matrix representation M is invertible.

bijective_injective_fact.label: Injective Condition
bijective_injective_fact.summary: L is injective if and only if ker L = {0}.

bijective_surjective_fact.label: Surjective Condition
bijective_surjective_fact.summary: L is surjective if and only if im L = W.

mat_theory.label: Matrix Theory
mat_theory.summary: The study of matrices as operators, including decompositions and inverses.

mat_ops.label: Matrix Operations
mat_ops.summary: Basic operations including multiplication, transpose, and trace.

trace_identity.label: Trace Identity
trace_identity.summary: The trace of a product is invariant under cyclic permutations: tr(MN) = tr(NM).

commute_fact.label: Matrix Commutativity
commute_fact.summary: In general, matrix multiplication is not commutative: AB != BA.

mat_decomp.label: Matrix Decompositions
mat_decomp.summary: Breaking a matrix into simpler constituent matrices to ease computation.

lu_decomp.label: LU Decomposition
lu_decomp.summary: Decomposing M into a Lower triangular (L) and Upper triangular (U) matrix to solve Mx = b via forward and backward substitution.

qr_decomp.label: QR Decomposition
qr_decomp.summary: Decomposing M into an orthogonal matrix Q and an upper triangular matrix R using the Gram-Schmidt process.

ldu_block.label: Block LDU Decomposition
ldu_block.summary: Applying decomposition to block matrices where components are themselves matrices.

mat_inverses.label: Matrix Inverses
mat_inverses.summary: The inverse M^-1 satisfies M M^-1 = I. For a 2x2 matrix, the inverse is (1/det M) * [d -b; -c a].

inv_prod_fact.label: Inverse of Product
inv_prod_fact.summary: The inverse of a product is the product of the inverses in reverse order: (AB)^-1 = B^-1 A^-1.

mat_exp.label: Matrix Exponential
mat_exp.summary: Defined by the power series exp(M) = I + M + M^2/2! + M^3/3! + ...

det_theory.label: Determinant Theory
det_theory.summary: A scalar value that characterizes several properties of a square matrix, including invertibility.

det_calc.label: Determinant Calculation
det_calc.summary: Methods for calculating the determinant of n x n matrices.

expansion_minors.label: Expansion by Minors
expansion_minors.summary: Calculating the determinant using a row or column, multiplying entries by their cofactors.

recursive_formula.label: Recursive Determinant Formula
recursive_formula.summary: Defining det(A) as the sum of elements times the determinants of their minors with alternating signs.

row_swap_det.label: Row Swap Effect
row_swap_det.summary: Swapping two rows flips the sign of the determinant.

row_scale_det.label: Row Scaling Effect
row_scale_det.summary: Multiplying a row by scalar lambda multiplies the determinant by lambda.

row_add_det.label: Row Addition Effect
row_add_det.summary: Adding a multiple of one row to another does not change the determinant.

det_invertibility.label: Determinants and Invertibility
det_invertibility.summary: A square matrix M is invertible if and only if det(M) != 0.

eigen_basics.label: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
eigen_basics.summary: An eigenvector v satisfies Mv = lambda*v, where lambda is the eigenvalue.

eigenspace.label: Eigenspace
eigenspace.summary: The subspace consisting of all eigenvectors associated with a specific eigenvalue lambda, plus the zero vector.

char_poly.label: Characteristic Polynomial
char_poly.summary: The polynomial P(lambda) = det(lambda*I - M), whose roots are the eigenvalues of M.

diag_condition.label: Diagonalizability Condition
diag_condition.summary: A matrix is diagonalizable if it has a complete set of linearly independent eigenvectors.

jordan_cells.label: Jordan Canonical Form
jordan_cells.summary: A representation for non-diagonalizable matrices using Jordan cells (diagonal with 1s on the super-diagonal).

inner_prod.label: Inner Product Spaces
inner_prod.summary: Vector spaces equipped with an inner product (dot product) allowing for the definition of length and angle.

orthogonality.label: Orthogonality
orthogonality.summary: Two vectors are orthogonal if their inner product is zero.

gram_schmidt.label: Gram-Schmidt Process
gram_schmidt.summary: A method for orthonormalizing a set of vectors by iteratively subtracting projections.

gs_formula.label: Gram-Schmidt Formula
gs_formula.summary: v_perp = v - sum((v . u_i) / (u_i . u_i)) * u_i

orthonormal_basis.label: Orthonormal Basis
orthonormal_basis.summary: A basis where all vectors are mutually orthogonal and have unit length.

apps_lin_alg.label: Applications of Linear Algebra
apps_lin_alg.summary: Applying linear algebraic concepts to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

fibonacci_mat.label: Fibonacci Sequence Matrix
fibonacci_mat.summary: Using a matrix M to represent the Fibonacci recursion X_{n+1} = M X_n, leading to Binet's formula via diagonalization.

conic_sections.label: Conic Sections
conic_sections.summary: Quadratic forms (X^T M X + ... = 0) representing circles, ellipses, hyperbolas, or lines based on eigenvalues.

least_squares.label: Least Squares Solutions
least_squares.summary: Finding an approximate solution to an overdetermined system by minimizing the squared error: M^T M a = M^T V.

vandermonde_det.label: Vandermonde Determinant
vandermonde_det.summary: The determinant of a Vandermonde matrix is the product of all pairs (x_i - x_j) for i > j.
